record.paper_title: Heavy flavors and quarkonia: highlights, open questions, and perspectives
record.original_question: In non-central ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collisions, heavy charm quarks can retain an early electromagnetic-field kick, and the charge-dependent directed flow Δv1 of D0 mesons relative to the spectator plane is used to calibrate the magnetic-field strength and lifetime. Why do RHIC and LHC measurements of the D0-meson charge splitting show different magnitudes and an opposite Δv1 slope, and does the opposite sign at the LHC relative to model calculations indicate that the Lorentz force is stronger than the Coulomb force for charm quarks?

evidence.quote: One of the observables that can be used to calibrate the strength and lifetime of the magnetic field is the charge dependence of the produced particle directed flow relative to the spectator plane, the so called Δv1 [1].

Experimental results at the RHIC by the STAR Collaboration and at the LHC by the ALICE Collaboration have shown indications for a different magnitude of the signal and an opposite slope of the Δv1 [2, 3].

The dependence of the charge splitting on collision energy is predicted to be mostly flat and negative [4], in contrast to the experimental findings. The opposite sign of the measured D0 meson Δv1 slope at the LHC with respect to model calculations might indicate a stronger effect of the Lorentz force relative to the Coulomb one. However, the experimental measurements are not yet fully significant due to the large uncertainties and did not allow for drawing firm conclusions.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider non-central ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collisions, in which the rapid relative motion of the spectator protons produces transient electromagnetic fields. Heavy charm quarks, created at very early times, can retain a kick from these fields. For neutral D mesons, define the charge-dependent directed flow with respect to the spectator plane as

Δv₁(y) = v₁(D⁰; y) − v₁(D̄⁰; y),

where v₁(y) = ⟨cos(φ − Ψ_SP)⟩ is the first Fourier coefficient of the azimuthal distribution as a function of rapidity y, measured relative to the spectator reaction plane Ψ_SP. The slope dΔv₁/dy near mid-rapidity is taken as a probe of the magnitude and lifetime of the early-time electromagnetic field experienced by charm quarks, where the Coulomb force from the long-lived electric field of receding spectators competes with the Lorentz force from the induced magnetic field.

Experimental measurements at top RHIC energies (√s_NN ≈ 200 GeV in Au+Au collisions) and at LHC energies (√s_NN ≈ 5.02 TeV in Pb+Pb collisions) report Δv₁ slopes that differ in both magnitude and sign, whereas state-of-the-art transport/electromagnetic-field model calculations predict an approximately flat, negative dependence on collision energy.

Problem. Provide a quantitative theoretical explanation, with statistical significance comparable to or exceeding the experimental uncertainties, for:

(a) the difference in magnitude of dΔv₁/dy between RHIC and LHC energies;
(b) the apparent opposite sign of the slope at the two energies;
(c) whether the observed sign reversal at the LHC, opposite to the model prediction, can be unambiguously attributed to the Lorentz force on charm quarks dominating over the Coulomb force, and if so, determine the corresponding constraint on the electrical conductivity and lifetime of the QGP electromagnetic field.
artifact.category_tag: heavy-ion electromagnetic fields and heavy-quark transport
artifact.status_search_result: Recent works (2021–2026) on directed flow of D mesons at RHIC and LHC continue to debate the mechanism. Models with standard electromagnetic profiles can reproduce the STAR Δv₁ at √s_NN = 200 GeV but fail to reproduce the much larger, positive-slope Δv₁ at LHC energies. Ongoing studies invoke non-constant conductivity, chirally conductive QGP, and longitudinal bulk-charm asymmetries, indicating the question is not yet resolved; experimental significance is also still limited.

status_evidence.title: Directed flow of D mesons at RHIC and LHC: non-perturbative dynamics, longitudinal bulk matter asymmetry and electromagnetic fields
status_evidence.snippet: At LHC standard electromagnetic profile assuming constant conductivity is not able to account for the huge splitting observed.
status_evidence.claim: Standard EM-field models cannot account for the LHC Δv₁ magnitude, indicating the explanation is still being sought.

status_evidence.title: Directed Flow of D and B Mesons in an Electrically and Chirally Conductive QGP at LHC Energies
status_evidence.snippet: At LHC the slope of the directed flow splitting is positive and about three orders of magnitude larger than that of light charged hadrons.
status_evidence.claim: Recent (2026) modeling still attempts to reproduce the LHC Δv₁ slope, indicating the problem is open.

status_evidence.title: The influence of electromagnetic fields on the generation of the directed and elliptic flows of heavy quark in relativistic heavy-ion collisions
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the influence of EM fields on directed and elliptic flow of heavy quarks.
status_evidence.claim: Continued 2025 theoretical work indicates the issue remains under active investigation.
